00109e30.mechanism: u8 parameter plus a single `asm volatile ("nop");` statement before the test. The parameter yields `andi a0,a0,0xff`, GCC hoists it above both prologue stores, and the emitted nop is absorbed into the beqz delay slot (target word 5) so the `sd ra,8(sp)` store is not pulled into the delay slot. Exact.

0014b950.mechanism: single flat OR expression whose terms are spelled in the order param_2, (param_2+..-1)<<0x10, param_3<<0x20, (param_3+..-1)<<0x30 (permutation D,C,B,A of the 24 commutative orderings tried as v21..v44). That order reproduces the exact dsll32/dsra32 schedule and the two crossed or-accumulators.

001ac310.mechanism: Ghidra-style `puVar1 = param_1 + 3;` with stores at puVar1[0x52] and puVar1[0x53] (== param_1[0x55]/[0x56]) and the two loads written in source order `[1]` then `[2]`; GCC then emits the loads in target order (lw t6,8(s0) then lw t7,4(s0)) while storing through s1 at 0x148/0x14c.

001e7230.mechanism: one reused `s32 iVar1` drives both the word and the byte loop and the second loop also compares against -1; reusing a single counter is what lands the loop counter in $t6 (no asm pinning needed).

00242500.mechanism: store-then-call-then-load tail (`*(int *)(uVar1 + 0x2440) = iVar1; uVar1 = func_001058e8(); return *(int *)(uVar1 + 0x2440);`) lets GCC keep v0 live across the last call so `sw t7,0x2440(v0)` lands in that jal's delay slot. The accumulator lands in $t7 only when the accumulation is written as TWO statements - `iVar1 = *(int *)(uVar1 + 0x2440);` then `iVar1 = iVar1 + param_1;` - instead of the single expression; the one-statement form allocates it to $a0 (4 words off). No register pin is needed: this compiler rejects `register x asm("$t7"/"t7"/"7"/"$7")` outright.
